episode_title: Your Window on the World of Innovation
question: What is Tarpeyo and how did it achieve FDA approval through an innovative two-step trial design?
transcript_excerpt: Tarpeyo is a drug developed by Caliditas Therapeutics that promises to revolutionize the treatment of a specific kidney disease and significantly reduce loss of kidney function. Caliditas was the first company globally allowed to run a pivotal trial with a two-step design using a surrogate marker—reduction of proteinuria—which led to accelerated approval, followed by longer-term data to achieve full approval based on kidney function endpoints in March 2023.

episode_title: Your Window on the World of Innovation
question: Why did Jenny McKenzie become passionate about literacy advocacy and educational reform?
transcript_excerpt: Jenny McKenzie was diagnosed with dyslexia at age 14 and was a student who hoped teachers would not call on her in class. She was fortunate to have parents who could access resources and support that changed her life, but she emphasizes this opportunity is not available to many people in the country and beyond, making reading and literacy deeply personal to her.

episode_title: Your Window on the World of Innovation
question: How can AI tools improve intellectual property work and legal decision-making in trademark and infringement cases?
transcript_excerpt: AI tools increase the quality of work and decision-making by broadening the scope beyond human bias. While humans are biased toward particular ways of looking at search or watch issues and focus on factors they think are most important, AI systems help identify every argument that could be made and pick out subtle details that humans are less capable of detecting, similar to how AI chess players outperform humans.

episode_title: Your Window on the World of Innovation
question: Why should legal professionals and IP experts actively participate in AI development conversations?
transcript_excerpt: Legal professionals, innovators, and IP community members should not be afraid to engage in conversations about AI and have an active role in steering its development because they are ultimately the people who will have to use it. Having a seat at the table to participate in those conversations is important, rather than having an AI system imposed on them.
